summary: Announces that two new Telnet options have been specified: Negotiate About Output Line Width (NAOL) and Negotiate About Output Page Size (NAOP). It names the NIC documents and the people who prepared them and put them on-line.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 587 announces two new Telnet options: one about output line width and one about output page size. It gives their names and NIC record numbers but does not describe how they work.

subtitle: An announcement of two newly specified Telnet options.

tldr.problem: The announcement reports the specification of two new Telnet options concerning output line width and page size.
tldr.mechanism: The options are named Negotiate About Output Line Width (NAOL) and Negotiate About Output Page Size (NAOP).

today: RFC 587 is an announcement of two Telnet option specifications and their associated NIC records.

sections.title: Two Telnet Options
sections.content: The RFC announces that two Telnet options have been specified: Negotiate About Output Line Width (NAOL), listed as NIC 20196, and Negotiate About Output Page Size (NAOP), listed as NIC 20197.
sections.plainLanguage: The announcement names two options, one for output line width and one for output page size. It points readers to the NIC records for their specifications.

sections.title: Preparation and Publication
sections.content: The options were prepared by Dave Walden of BBN-NET and put online by Anita Coley and Dave Crocker of UCLA-NMC. RFC 587 does not provide option formats, negotiation steps or detailed behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: The note credits the people who prepared and published the option specifications. It does not explain their technical details.

sections.title: Scope of This Note
sections.content: This RFC is an announcement rather than the specifications themselves. It identifies the two option names and the NIC numbers associated with their documents.
sections.plainLanguage: Use this note to identify the two options and their records, not as a description of their operation.
